items.subject: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, seeking relaxation in the time period stipulated under Regulation 8.2(c) of the said Regulations for submission of the Connectivity Bank Guarantees against Intimation of In-Principle Grant of Connectivity (Intimation No. CTU/S/5/Conn/INT-1A-2200001607 dated 27.03.2026), condonation of the delay of two (2) days in submission of such Bank Guarantees, and a direction to Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to take the said Bank Guarantees on record and issue the Final Grant of Connectivity for 100 MW (with 50 MW BESS) at NP Kunta Pooling Station, Andhra Pradesh. Pace Digitek Limited

- b) Pursuant to the in-principle Grant of Connectivity, and well within the prescribed period, the Petitioner promptly initiated the process for issuance of the Conn-BGs

c) On 16.04.2026, the Petitioner addressed a communication to CTUIL seeking the prescribed BG format. CTUIL responded by the end of the day, forwarding the format available on the CTUIL website. On 17.04.2026, CTUIL addressed a reminder to the Petitioner to submit the Conn BGs. On 23.04.2026, i.e., four (4) days prior to the prescribed deadline, the Petitioner caused Canara Bank to purchase the requisite non-judicial e-Stamp papers for issuance of the Conn-BGs.

d) On 24.04.2026, the Petitioner, three (3) days before the prescribed deadline, submitted the draft BG (in the original 2 years + 6 months format) to CTUIL for vetting. By email of the same date, CTUIL conveyed that the draft was not in conformity with the prescribed format inasmuch as the tenor was required to be 3 years + 1 year claim period, and forwarded a modified draft.

- b) It is prayed that the Commission may take the present affidavit on record along with the annexure and treat the closure letter dated 19.05.2025 as an additional impugned communication forming part of the subject matter of the accompanying Petition.

- e) On 21.05.2026, the Petitioner filed a Writ Petition being Writ Petition No. 7344/2026 before the High Court of Delhi seeking quashing of the above Closure Letter dated 19.05.2026 issued by CTUIL. On 22.05.2026, the matter was heard by the Delhi High Court, where the Writ Petition was disposed of while directing that the communication dated 19.05.2026 not be given effect to till the time the present Petition filed by the petitioner along with an application for interim stay before this Commission is taken up for consideration. The Delhi High Court clarified that the order had been passed without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case.

10. Petitioner, vide Affidavit dated 26.06.2026, filed a rejoinder to the CTUIL reply and mainly submitted as below:

- a) The Petitioner has entered into a Power Purchase Agreement dated 24.10.2024 with SECI, under which the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date is 27.09.2026. Given the strict implementation milestones stipulated under the PPA, the Petitioner is already working within compressed timelines. It is therefore imperative that this Commission direct CTUIL to forthwith restore the Petitioner's connectivity. To date, the Petitioner has committed an amount of approximately ₹557.62 crore, including the execution of Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) Contracts, towards the development and commissioning of the Project.

12. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondents and perused the Regulatory provisions and the facts available on the record. The issue which arises for our consideration is whether the Petitioner's case is a fit case for the exercise of power under Regulations 41 (Power to Relax) and 42 (Power to Remove Difficulty) of the GNA Regulations to condone the two-day delay in the submission of Con-BGs. The issue is discussed in the subsequent paragraphs.

14. Petitioner has submitted that the present case is squarely covered by the Commission’s order dated 25.3.2025 in Petition No. 89/MP/2025 (Tata Power Renewable Energy Ltd. v. CTUIL) wherein the Commission, in exercise of its powers under Regulations 41 and 42, condoned a delay of four days in the submission of Conn BGs and directed CTUIL to accept the same.

As per the above, CTUIL stated that the Petitioner is a defaulter in terms of the intimation dated 27.03.2026 and remains liable for appropriate action as per the GNA Regulations.

# 19. We have also perused the Order dated 25.03.2025 in Petition No. 89/MP/2025 quoted

_28.We are of the considered view that the delay in submission of Conn BGs was unintentional and inadvertent. Further, compliance was expeditious therefore, we find the case of the Petitioner a fit case to be considered for relaxation to remove the hardship to the applicant that would arise with revocation of in-principle connectivity granted to the Petitioner._

Petitioner is a fit case for relaxation to remove the hardship that would arise with the revocation of the in-principle grant of Connectivity.

25. Petition No. 241/MP/2026 along with IA No. 77/2026 is disposed of in terms of the above.
